title: Flexible Seismicity Modeling With Neural Modulated Renewal Processes
content:
Abstract

Neural point processes (NPPs) have recently been applied to seismicity modeling, but their theoretical connections to classical point processes models remain elusive. Moreover, two fundamental questions remain unresolved: (a) how much historical information is sufficient for NPPs to effectively model seismicity, and (b) what is the differential impact between inter-event times and magnitudes on the model predictive performance? To answer these questions, we reinterpret a class of NPPs within the framework of neural modulated renewal processes (NMRPs), which generalize conventional modulated renewal processes by integrating deep learning architectures. We develop and analyze four variants: the unmodulated neural renewal process (NRP), the inter-event times modulated NMRP (I-NMRP), the magnitude modulated NMRP (M-NMRP), and the jointly modulated NMRP (J-NMRP). Their performance is systematically evaluated against the epidemic-type aftershock sequence (ETAS) model using the EarthquakeNPP benchmark. Results demonstrate that I-NMRP and J-NMRP not only match, but in some cases surpass, ETAS in terms of log-likelihood, while requiring substantially less historical input. Furthermore, the analysis reveals that inter-event times play a more critical role than magnitudes in enhancing predictive performance. These findings establish NMRP as a flexible and efficient framework for seismicity modeling, with strong potential to incorporate diverse contextual information and to deepen our understanding of earthquake triggering processes.
